title: Auth Control Plane security audit event (v1 wire format)
description:
One row of security_audit_events (TRD sections 9 and 13) as it crosses a service boundary. The audit trail is append-only and its metadata is ALLOWLISTED and secret-free: never plaintext secrets, raw codes, provider tokens, untrusted bodies or high-cardinality identities. A schema cannot assert "no secrets"; it can make the fields that would carry them unrepresentable, so `attributes` is a closed object of typed members and an arbitrary key fails. The table's client_ip and free-text request detail are deliberately NOT carried: an address is a high-cardinality identity, and the database column stays in the database.

`outcome` is closed (allowed, denied, error) so the trail can be aggregated and alerted on. `policy_revision` names which policy produced a decision (ACP-ADR-05) and is an integer token in 0..2^53-1 (refused on the raw token when written in decimal form), like every wire integer (see provisioning-event.v1).

event_type.description: What happened, from the producer's closed vocabulary (text in the database so adding one is not a migration).

actor_principal_id.description: Who did it. Absent for events with no actor (a failed login for an unknown identity).

subject_principal_id.description: Who it was done to. Differs from the actor for administrative actions; collapsing them loses what an investigation needs.

reason_code.description: A reason code from a CLOSED vocabulary (contracts/auth/v1/vocabulary/reason-codes.json): the codes used by authorization decisions and error.v1 in this corpus, the revoked_reason values, and the reason codes the merged audit producer accepts. A pattern would admit a secret-shaped lowercase value, so the set is an enum. A new value arrives with the producer that emits it.

resource_type.description: An unknown resource type is a denial (TRD section 14), so the vocabulary is closed.

attributes.description: The allowlist. Adding a member is a contract change reviewed as one.
